clue.text: Leader of the fleet gets tired with it

parts.note: to flag is to tire or lose energy
hip means fashionable, with it

explanation.surface: A lead ship is worn out alongside the rest of the fleet.
explanation.definitionFit: The flagship carries the admiral and heads a naval squadron.

clue.text: Tamper with instrument

explanation.definitionFit: To fiddle is to meddle or interfere with something; a fiddle is a violin, a musical instrument.

clue.text: A lower storey represents a demotion

parts.note: a basement is the storey below ground level

explanation.surface: Being moved down to a lower floor is a sign of losing rank.
explanation.definitionFit: Abasement is humiliation or lowering in rank, as a demotion is.

clue.text: Stops in the street, say, when confused

parts.note: ST is the usual abbreviation for street

indicators.note: confused signals that the letters of the word say are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone halts in the road and, bewildered, speaks.
explanation.definitionFit: Stays as a verb means halts or stops, as in staying an execution.

clue.text: Deeply emotional in future perhaps

parts.note: the future is an example of a grammatical tense

explanation.surface: Someone imagines strong feelings in the days to come.
explanation.definitionFit: Intense feelings are strong and passionate ones.

clue.text: Good losers left in two set-ends

indicators.note: in signals that one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: the end letter of sets at each side, or the start of set taken twice, gives two S letters
port is the left side of a ship

explanation.surface: A tennis match where the beaten player stays gracious through two closing sets.
explanation.walkthrough: PORT goes inside S...S; the two S letters come from 'two set-ends', read as the end letters of sets.
explanation.definitionFit: Good sports are people who accept defeat graciously.

clue.text: Fail exam, take degree, start to niggle farm worker

parts.note: to plough is old British student slang for failing an exam
MA, Master of Arts, is a university degree

indicators.note: start to means only the opening letter of niggle is used

explanation.surface: A student flunks, takes a degree, and begins to grumble about life on the farm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plough' meaning to fail an exam is dated British university slang.
explanation.definitionFit: A ploughman tills the fields, so he is a labourer on the land.

clue.text: Respond to stimulus and race off on time

indicators.note: off signals that the letters of race are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: A runner reacts to the starting gun and sets off punctually.
explanation.walkthrough: 'race off' reads like a sprint start, but 'off' is the anagram signal; 'on' places the time letter after the jumble in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: To react is to behave in response to some stimulus.

clue.text: She left nothing on cricket pitch for web-footed bird

parts.note: a duck is a batsman's score of zero in cricket

explanation.surface: A woman walked off the cricket field, leaving behind a bird with webbed feet.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a batsman out without scoring is 'out for a duck'.
explanation.definitionFit: The shelduck is a large waterfowl of the duck family, with webbed feet.

clue.text: Young woman backs stake with artificial jewels

indicators.note: backs signals that the word for young woman is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: a maid is a girl or young woman
an ante is a poker player's stake

explanation.surface: A girl bets on fake gems.
explanation.definitionFit: Diamante is costume jewellery of glittering imitation stones.

clue.text: Give university fellow a note

parts.note: a don is a fellow or tutor at a university, especially Oxford or Cambridge
te is a note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Hand an academic a written message.
explanation.definitionFit: To donate is to give money or goods to a cause.

clue.text: Never climbing, endlessly flat

indicators.note: climbing in a down clue means the letters are read upwards, backwards
endlessly means the final letter of never is removed

explanation.surface: Something that never rises stays level forever.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts NEVER to NEVE; 'climbing' turns that upwards in the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: An even surface is smooth and level, without bumps.

clue.text: Northern city in Dales Borders on sheltered side

indicators.note: on means the second piece comes after the first

parts.note: the lee is the side sheltered from the wind

indicators.note: borders means the outer letters of Dales, its first and last

explanation.surface: A northern town found sheltered in the Yorkshire Dales.
explanation.walkthrough: The Dales are hill country in northern England; LEEDS is a city in Yorkshire.
explanation.definitionFit: Leeds is a large city in Yorkshire, in the north of England.

clue.text: Took the correct course in vain, wrongly kept in

indicators.note: wrongly signals that the letters of vain are mixed up

parts.note: gated means confined to college or school as a punishment

explanation.surface: A pupil found the right way but was kept in after school anyway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in vain' tempts as a phrase, but 'in' is a link; 'wrongly' turns VAIN into NAVI. Being 'gated' is British school slang for detention.
explanation.definitionFit: To navigate is to plot and steer the right route.

clue.text: Seeds from Home Counties identical

parts.note: the Home Counties around London lie in the South East, SE
same means identical

explanation.surface: Seed packets from the countryside near London all look alike.
explanation.walkthrough: The Home Counties are the counties surrounding London, in South East England.
explanation.definitionFit: Sesame is a plant grown for its small edible oily seeds.

clue.text: A health resort has rejected sweetener on succulent shoots

parts.note: a spa is a resort with mineral springs

indicators.note: rejected means the sweetener word is turned back to front

parts.note: sugar is a sweetener

explanation.surface: A spa refuses to put sugar on its vegetable dishes.
explanation.definitionFit: Asparagus is eaten as its young tender stems, a vegetable delicacy.

clue.text: Dominican not in, moving about, wandering

indicators.note: moving about signals that the letters of Dominican, once in is taken out, are rearranged

explanation.surface: A Dominican friar is never at home, always on the road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not in' removes I and N from DOMINICAN; 'moving about' rearranges the rest (DOMICA N).
explanation.definitionFit: Nomadic people roam from place to place without fixed homes.

clue.text: The race is behind a barrier. Blast it!

indicators.note: is behind means the race word follows the barrier word

parts.note: a dam is a barrier holding back water
a nation is a people or race

explanation.surface: A runner stuck behind a hurdle curses.
explanation.definitionFit: Damnation is used as an exclamation of anger, like a curse.

clue.text: Following Morse, perhaps every address should have one

parts.note: post means after, as in postwar
Morse is an example of a code

explanation.surface: After the telegraph era, every home needs an identifier for mail.
explanation.definitionFit: A postcode is the letters and numbers added to a postal address for sorting mail.

clue.text: After a month, work with creature of the deep

indicators.note: after means the work comes after the month

parts.note: Oct is short for October
an opus is a work, especially a musical composition

explanation.surface: After a month, a diver works alongside a sea creature.
explanation.definitionFit: The octopus is an eight-armed sea animal.

clue.text: Small sweet potato

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as in clothing sizes
pud, short for pudding, is a British word for a sweet course

explanation.surface: A little sweet potato.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sweet potato' looks like one vegetable; 'sweet' is the pudding and 'potato' the definition. In Britain 'sweet' and 'pud' both mean dessert.
explanation.definitionFit: Spud is an informal word for a potato.

clue.text: Criticise a mother's hat

parts.note: to pan is to criticise harshly
ma is mother; the 's stands for is

explanation.surface: Someone mocks their mum's headwear.
explanation.definitionFit: A Panama is a brimmed straw sun-hat.

clue.text: Goes around selling bicycle parts by the sound of it

indicators.note: by the sound of it means the word for bicycle parts is heard, not seen

parts.note: pedals are the parts of a bicycle pushed by the feet

explanation.surface: A hawker cycles round the town flogging wares.
explanation.definitionFit: A pedlar peddles, travelling about to sell goods.

clue.text: Rodent eats top of sweet, creamy dessert

indicators.note: eats means the rodent takes another piece inside it

parts.note: a mouse is a rodent

indicators.note: top of means the first letter of sweet, in this down clue

explanation.surface: A mouse nibbles at a creamy pudding.
explanation.definitionFit: Mousse is a light whipped pudding, often chocolate.

clue.text: Switch group's drinks to face the other way

parts.note: to switch is to turn, change direction
a round is a set of drinks bought for a group

explanation.surface: A barman swaps the group's drinks order.
explanation.definitionFit: To turn round is to rotate so as to face backwards.

clue.text: Are almost all races to be found in this country

indicators.note: to be found in signals that the letters lie inside the words Are almost

explanation.surface: Nearly every race can be found in this nation.
explanation.definitionFit: A realm is a kingdom, a country under a monarch.

clue.text: Piaf cut short number played on this?

indicators.note: cut short means the last letter of Piaf is dropped

explanation.surface: A chanson by Edith Piaf, abbreviated, performed at the keyboard.
explanation.walkthrough: Edith Piaf was a French singer; 'cut short' drops her name's last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A piano is an instrument on which a musical number may be performed.

clue.text: Awkward question for photographer's sitter

explanation.definitionFit: A poser is a puzzling problem; a poser is also someone who poses for a portrait.

clue.text: Colour of old cooking stove

parts.note: a range is a large kitchen stove

explanation.surface: The paint shade of an antique kitchen oven.
explanation.definitionFit: Orange is a hue between red and yellow.

clue.text: Latin and Greek courses run by three-year-olds

explanation.walkthrough: In British racing the Classics are five famous flat races open only to three-year-old horses.
explanation.definitionFit: Classics is the study of ancient Greek and Latin; the Classics are five major British flat horse races for three-year-old thoroughbreds, such as the Derby.

clue.text: To entangle men, she changed

indicators.note: changed signals that the letters of men and she are rearranged

explanation.surface: A woman alters the menfolk to ensnare them.
explanation.definitionFit: To enmesh is to catch as in a net, to tangle up.

clue.text: Antagonise Greens at resort

indicators.note: resort is read as re-sort, to sort the letters of Greens at again

explanation.surface: Environmental campaigners upset people at a holiday resort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resort' looks like a holiday place but reads as 're-sort'.
explanation.definitionFit: To estrange is to alienate someone, making them hostile.
